message.content:
This looks like a CBP ruling on herbal tinctures made from several botanicals. The relevant heading is 1302 (vegetable saps and extracts), specifically 1302.19 (other).

The subheading 1302.19 is split into 1302.19.05 (of a kind used primarily in pharmacy), 1302.19.15 (other), and so on. The HTSUS breaks down as follows:
- 1302.11 is opium.
- 1302.12 is licorice.
- 1302.13 is hops.
- 1302.14 is pyrethrum or derris.
- 1302.19 is other.
  - 1302.19.05: Medicinal.
  - 1302.19.10: Ginseng extracts.
  - 1302.19.15: Other, including those used in food flavors.
  - 1302.19.21 and 1302.19.40: Other.

I recall the subheadings as 1302.19.05 (containing mixtures, with 1302.19.0500 "Medicinal"), 1302.19.15 (for 1302.19.15 "Of a kind used primarily in pharmacy" with 1302.19.1500), 1302.19.20 (ginseng) and 1302.19.40 (other). I'm not certain of these breakdowns, so I'm choosing 1302.19.9100 as a safe general "other" option. The actual structure has 1302.19.91 for "Other: Other" in the "Other" group, and 1302.19.4100 for "Other" as well, which I'm not sure about.

I'll go with the medicinal-use option, 1302.19.4000, though an alternative would be 1302.19.9190.

Classification is under heading 1302, with an uncertain choice among the statistical suffixes.
